la:verb:eblandior.html:
ē-blandĭor, ītus, 4,
v. dep. a., to obtain by flattery or coaxing (rare but class.): enitere, elabora vel potius eblandire, effice, ut, etc., C, § 12; cf. ; : unum consulatus diem,: solitudinem ruris,.—
Of inanimate subjects, to foster, mature by mildness: caelo fecunditatem omnem eblandito,; cf. ; and somewhat diferently: ut eblandiatur lac igneam saevitiam,

i. e. mitigate and drive it out, .!*? Part., eblandītus, a, um, pass., obtained or caught by flattery: eblandita suffragia,; cf. preces,: aures nostrae,.

la:adj:ebrius.html:
ēbrĭus, a, um, adj.
etym. dub.; perh. root φρήν; cf. sobrius
,
who has drunk enough, had his fill, corresp. with satur.
Prop. (very rare): cum tu satura atque ebria eris, puer ut satur sit facito, Ruhnk.; cf. saturitate,.—Far more freq. and class.,
full of drink, drunk, intoxicated (cf. also: potus, ebriosus, temulentus, vinolentus): homo hic ebrius est ... Tu istic, ubi bibisti?; ; , sq. al.; ; ; ; (thrice); ; ; ; ; .— As subst.: ebrĭus, ii, m., a drunkard, ; id. Job, 12, 25 al. et saep.—
Poet., of inanimate things: vestigia,; cf. signa, (4, 2, 48 M.): verba,: nox,; cf. bruma, et saep.—
Trop., intoxicated, drunk, sated, filled: ebrius jam sanguine civium et tanto magis eum sitiens,: regina fortuna dulci ebria,intoxicated with good fortune,: dulcis pueri ebrios ocellos,i. e. intoxicated with love,: ebria de sanguine sanctorum,.—
In gen., abundantly filled, full (poet.): cena,: lana de sanguine conchae,; cf. : lucerna,.

la:verb:ebibo.html:
ē-bĭbo, bi, bĭtum, 3, v. a.,
to drink up, drain (not in Cic. or Caes.).
Lit.: quid comedent? quid ebibent?; so with comedere,; ; hirneam vini,: poculum,: ubera lactantia, et saep.: elephantos dracones,i. e. to suck their blood,; cf. sanguinem,: cum vino simitu imperium,to drink up, forget through drinking, (cf. in the simplex: bibere mandata,, v. bibo).—Poet.: invenies illic, qui Nestoris ebibat annos, to drink the age of Nestor (i. e. to drink as many glasses as equal the years of Nestor), . —
Transf., of inanimate things, to suck in, draw in, absorb: (fretum) peregrinos amnes,; cf. : saniem (lana),.—
In gen., to waste in drink, squander, . —
Trop., to exhaust, remove, take away: spiritum meum,.

la:verb:ebullio.html:
ē-bullĭo, īre, 4 (and post-class. ēbullo, āre, 1), v. n. and a.
Neutr., to boil up, bubble up (post-class.).
Lit.: fontium venae ebullant,.—
Trop., to come forth bubbling, to appear boisterously: dum risus ebullit .—Poet.: o si Ebullit patrui praeclarum funus! i. e. utinam patruus moriatur, Dübner: priusquam hujus monstri idoli artifices ebullissent,: de Perside,to hurry confusedly away, Mac. 1, 12.—
Act. (class., but rare).
Lit.: animam,i. e. to breathe out, give up the ghost,; ; .—
To produce in abundance: et ebulliet fluvius ranas,; cf.: os fatuorum ebullit stultitiam,.—Trop.: virtutes,i. e. to boast of, Kühn; cf. (and the Gr. παφλάζειν).
